description: GROUNDING GATE - consumed ONLY by tools/check_grounding.py; NEVER sent to the Anthropic API (it is not part of the rendered prompt bundle). Each entry names a grounding concept that MUST survive into the rendered bundle so a future API run reproduces the same behavior. This catches the one failure a forward config->prompt check cannot: a concept deleted from config entirely, or only ever written into an agent-only doc (SKILL.md). TWO KINDS OF PIN: (1) REFERENCE-BASED - `source` points at the config field that OWNS the rule; the gate asserts that field exists (catches deletion) and its text reaches the rendered bundle. No rule text is copied here, so the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH stays in defects.json / parts/*.json and cannot drift out of sync with a copied phrase. (2) LITERAL - `must_contain` phrase, used ONLY for grounding that lives in freeform prose with no field path (system_prompt.md universals, and part rulings/notes arrays). When you harden grounding, prefer a `source` reference; fall back to `must_contain` only for freeform prose.

required.why: Generalizes the gestalt-skip fix to the WHOLE position-agnostic surface-blemish family (line_mark, dark_spot, dark_mark, white_mark, dent, edge_chip, corrosion) on EVERY part, not just dark on the bracket. Forces a per-ZONE enumerated sweep (face, every edge/rim, every hole border) so OK cannot be returned by a whole-part glance. Roots out the 164818 miss (a faint top-edge dark_spot skipped because the part looked clean). Universal system_prompt prose - pinned by phrase so it reaches both prompts.
must_contain: ZONE SWEEP FOR SURFACE DEFECTS
OK is invalid unless every zone is explicitly cleared

required.why: Supplies the bracket's part-specific zone list (open face, top edge, bottom edge, each end, each of the 3 hole borders) for the universal ZONE SWEEP, clearing the whole surface-blemish family per zone - not a dark-only check. Pinned so the zone list reaches both prompts and can never be dropped.
must_contain: SURFACE SWEEP ZONES
may NOT be returned OK unless this surface_sweep lists ALL of the above zones EXPLICITLY CLEARED

required.why: LLM bbox coordinates are perceptual ESTIMATES, imprecise at the exact edge (a left edge read as 0.40 when the defect starts at 0.47). A labeled coordinate-grid copy of the input is attached (inspect._bundle_images via grid.grid_for) and the engine must READ each bbox edge off the nearest gridline instead of guessing a fraction. Pinned so the grid-reading rule reaches the future API and can never be dropped. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: READ COORDINATES OFF THE GRID
take the NUMBERS from the grid copy

required.why: The systematic miss: embossing_missing (an ABSENCE defect gated behind face classification) was silently skipped and the part defaulted to OK because nothing loud appeared. This forcing function makes OK impossible without a positive per-checkpoint clearance, and requires the prerequisite observation to run first. Must reach every part's prompt (and the future Anthropic API) so a silent skip cannot recur. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: POSITIVE CHECKPOINT CLEARANCE - `OK` IS NOT A DEFAULT
including ABSENCE defects

make that
  prerequisite observation FIRST, or the whole branch is silently skipped

required.why: The forcing function only works if the engine must EMIT the checkpoint results: `checkpoints` is a mandatory output field and OK is invalid unless every checkpoint is CLEARED. Pinned so the required-output contract reaches the future API and cannot be dropped from the prompt. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: `checkpoints` is MANDATORY

A `result` of `OK` is
INVALID unless every checkpoint is `CLEARED`

required.why: The fabrication miss: dark-mark boxes were typed from inference in a batch, landing OFF the part (on background) and as tiny sub-actionable specks, and several near-identical boxes collapsed together instead of one. This forcing function makes every bbox a claim about pixels actually seen - on the part, actionable, placed by looking - and requires a tight cluster to be ONE box. Must reach the future Anthropic API so a hallucinated/off-part/tiny box is never emitted. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: EVERY BBOX MUST BE VALID - ON THE PART, ACTIONABLE, AND PLACED BY LOOKING

a box on the background/paper, off the part edge, or on empty space is NEVER a
  real surface defect

emit ONE box covering the cluster, not several
  collapsing boxes

required.why: The recurring silent-skip: a defect type (line_mark, then embossing, then dark) defaulted to OK/omitted because no anomaly caught the eye. This master ruling enumerates EVERY checkpoint (face, serration, embossing, line_mark, dark, white, global) as a required `checkpoints` entry that gates OK, so no single defect type can be silently skipped. line_mark is named explicitly (the last miss). Pinned so the enumerated checklist reaches the future API and can never be dropped. Freeform part ruling - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: MANDATORY CHECKPOINT LIST (gates OK
line_mark - SWEEP THE WHOLE FACE for thin continuous grooves
Under-reporting a checkpoint you did not actively run is the same failure as a silent OK

required.why: Bracket-specific forcing function: the face+VA embossing checkpoint must run on EVERY image and gate OK, so a FRONT face with a blank VA can never be defaulted to OK (the exact miss). Pinned so the mandatory checkpoint reaches the future API and can never be dropped from the bracket rulings. Freeform part ruling - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: MANDATORY EMBOSSING CHECKPOINT (gates OK
a blank VA zone may NEVER be defaulted to OK without first CONFIRMING the BACK (square, sharp) edge profile

required.why: The renderer draws the serration locator CIRCLE inside the reported bbox; a loose/whole-part box makes the circle land on the wrong hole.

The recurring false positive (image 164209): a COUNTERSUNK/DISHED/DOMED serrated hole shows a smooth-looking bore and was flagged serration_missing at high confidence, when its RIM actually shows scallops (serration PRESENT). This directed two-pattern match (serrated scalloped rim vs plain smooth rim) forces the decision onto the RIM only and carries the countersink/dome guard, so a domed bore is never read as missing. Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.
The VA emboss zone is located by part geometry (between the middle hole and the plain end-hole, opposite the serrated hole); the box must be small and there, drawn box-only.

The 'VA' logo is stamped on the FRONT face ONLY. A blank VA zone means the BACK face is shown (normal), NOT embossing_missing - flagging a back-facing part as embossing_missing is a false positive (image 164359). Pinned so the front/back rule can never be dropped and reaches the future API. Freeform part ruling - pinned by phrase.
required.must_contain: the BACK face is shown and that is NORMAL

required.why: The face must be decided from the EDGE/ROUNDING PROFILE, independently of the 'VA', or embossing_missing can never fire: the old rule inferred the face from VA presence alone (circular), so a genuine FRONT face with a missing VA was wrongly passed as 'back face'. The FRONT (punch-entry) face has curved rolled 'sliding' bevelled edges (reference 164116); the BACK (die) face has flat sharp square edges (reference 164359). Pinned so this VA-independent discriminator reaches the future API and can never be dropped. Freeform part ruling - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: on the FRONT (punch-entry) face the outer edge is CHAMFERED / ROLLED-OVER
on the BACK (die) face the outer edge is SQUARE and SHARP

required.why: Confidence must be COMPUTED, not guessed. It is a weighted average of by-eye evidence factors (rim_smoothness 0.5, evidence_readability 0.3, anchor_certainty 0.2), so a crisp obviously-toothless bore scores HIGHER than a domed/glare-softened one (the 164017-vs-163907 inversion). Pinned so the scoring rubric reaches the future API and stays in sync with grounded_inspector/confidence.py's weights.
The renderer segments the dark pixels inside the reported bbox; the box must cover the full visible defect footprint or coherent cluster with a small margin, not tiny individual pixels.
Operator ground truth showed 2+ discrete dark spots per part; the engine under-counted (drew one broad box). Enumerate every discrete spot, one tight box each, including spots on the strap edges.
On iridescent brackets the engine flagged passivation tint / hole bores / diffuse haze as dark spots. A dark_spot must be a discrete clearly-bounded blemish, not tint/hole/haze.

A few isolated dark pixels without a visible surrounding footprint are not actionable dark spots. Keep them below the 0.60 confidence gate; annotate only a coherent defect-sized area and box its full visible footprint.

Day-to-day recall of faint edge/scatter dark spots was unstable because inspection was open-ended ('find the defects'). This directed protocol anchors dark_spot on the attached pattern crops and forces a zone-by-zone 'does any region match this pattern?' sweep (face + both edges + rim), listing EVERY match. Pilot for the pattern-matching approach; pinned so the protocol reaches the future API and can never be dropped.

Directed anatomy-agnostic pattern match rolled out to every global defect (stability over open-ended inspection). Anchors corrosion on its pattern and forces a zone-by-zone match sweep, listing every region that matches. Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.

Directed anatomy-agnostic pattern match for line_mark: zoom region-by-region and list every groove that matches the line pattern, so a faint groove is not skipped. Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.

Directed anatomy-agnostic pattern match for dent: trace the whole contour and list every broken-contour+depression region that matches the dent pattern. Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.

Directed anatomy-agnostic pattern match for edge_chip: trace the entire silhouette and list every missing-material break that matches the chip pattern. Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.

Directed anatomy-agnostic pattern match for dark_mark: zone-by-zone, list every near-black connected blotch that matches the pattern (and keep a scatter of separated specks as dark_spots). Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.

Directed anatomy-agnostic pattern match for white_mark: zone-by-zone, list every localised dull low-luster patch that matches the pattern (not glare, not uniform tint). Pinned so it reaches the future API and can never be dropped.
The operator-marked bracket shows a coherent localized matte/pale patch that must be reported as white_mark, not dismissed as glare or OK. The full visible patch must be boxed.
Operator: a dark_mark is an ABSOLUTE near-black area only; the rainbow passivation tint must never be marked. Can be one or multiple, each tight.

Operator-marked bracket references distinguish connected elongated smears, irregular patches, and touching dark clusters as one dark_mark, while dark_spot is reserved for separate small isolated specks. This prevents splitting one connected dark mark into several spot boxes.

Operator-labeled brackets show the real line marks are FAINT low-contrast grooves; the brightest bands (specular reflection / rim glare) are false positives. The engine must be told to reject the brightest band and hunt the fainter interior grooves, or it repeats the bright-band false positive.
Line marks are drawn as a BOX around the groove, not a stroked trace. Pinned so the box drawing discipline reaches both prompts and the future API and can never be dropped from config.
Faint grooves (images 734/750) are invisible at full-frame scale and were only found after zooming; the engine must zoom into suspect regions before concluding present/absent, or it repeats the miss.
Serration must be judged from the rim silhouette, not the bore brightness, so glare does not cause false serration_missing.

Generic (all-part) discipline must live in the shared system prompt, not only in a part's rulings, so a new part inherits it automatically and it never depends on the operator/agent re-deriving it. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - no field path, so pinned by phrase.
must_contain: ANCHOR ON ANATOMY, NOT THE FRAME

required.why: Every part on a bright/washed-out photo needs glare discipline; keep it generic in the system prompt so it is not lost when a part omits a per-defect glare_rule. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: GLARE / BRIGHT-FINISH DISCIPLINE
judge shape from the EDGE OUTLINE

required.why: The confidence gate / prefer-OK bias were being misread as a licence to report only the single most obvious instance of a repeating defect (line marks, dark spots), causing under-counts. This universal rule keeps count-first enumeration in the shared system prompt for EVERY part so a new part inherits it and the future API always receives it. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: ENUMERATE, DO NOT UNDER-COUNT
Reporting one when several exist is a FAILURE

required.why: The 0.60 annotate gate and prefer-OK bias are core to matching QMS results and must be in the bundle for every part, not just in SKILL.md or per-part rulings. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: Ignore/do not annotate any finding below 0.60 confidence
PREFER OK / NEEDS_REVIEW OVER A FALSE FLAG

required.why: The dent vs edge_chip vs missing_punch vs corrosion call is the decisive bearing-cup cue (missing material -> edge_chip; intact push-in -> dent; unpunched bore -> missing_punch). It lives in the part's notes and MUST reach BOTH single and auto prompts, or the API would confuse damage types. Freeform part note - no field path, so pinned by phrase.
must_contain: Missing/sheared material at the rim -> edge_chip. Metal pushed in but intact -> dent.

required.why: Tilted side-view cups with a smooth, partly-visible inner rim are OK; a speculative box is a false flag. This ruling must reach the bundle so the API does not over-mark tilted cups. Freeform part ruling - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: Tilted / side-view cups whose inner rim is smooth and not clearly visible are OK

required.why: Rim/edge defects need a TIGHT bbox on the actual defect (not the whole rim arc) so the renderer segments the right region. Freeform part ruling - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: use a TIGHT bbox on the actual defect, not the whole rim arc

required.why: Confidence was being assigned by peak brightness / how much a mark 'pops', which ranks a SHORT locally-bright groove above a LONG clearly-visible faint one (exactly the 163740-vs-163750 error). The durable, eye-aligned definition is CONTINUITY x LENGTH: how much unbroken plainly-visible groove there is. Pinned so the future Anthropic API scores line_mark confidence by visible groove length, not brightness.

The most common line_mark error is UNDER-COUNTING - reporting the single most obvious groove and silently dropping the fainter ones (exactly the bracket 163810/164510 miss). The confidence gate and prefer-OK bias were being misread as a licence to omit a faint-but-visible groove. This rule makes enumeration a COUNT-FIRST-then-trace discipline and states that low confidence LOWERS a mark's score or flags NEEDS_REVIEW, but NEVER deletes a visible groove. Pinned so the future Anthropic API always receives the anti-undercount discipline and it can never be dropped from config.

Line marks are drawn as TIGHT per-groove boxes and the count must match reality (e.g. part 003 has 4). The engine must emit one tight box per distinct line mark and never merge several grooves into one big box. Pinned so this box/counting discipline can never be dropped from config - the renderer draws exactly the boxes the verdict supplies. Guards the same annotation.instruction field as line_mark.box_annotation, for the counting concern.

COLOUR is the decisive line-vs-dark cue: a DARK / near-black mark is a dark_spot / dark_mark even when elongated; line_mark is reserved for BRIGHT / metallic exposed-metal scratches. This must reach BOTH prompts so the engine (and the future API) never labels a dark mark as a line_mark.

The reciprocal colour cue: any mark DARKER (near-black) than the finish is a dark_spot (or dark_mark), even if somewhat elongated - darkness wins over shape. Pinned so it can never be silently dropped.

edge_chip had NO localization rule, so the engine drew a box that drifted off the actual sheared/reddish rim spot. The renderer draws exactly the reported bbox, so this tight-localization instruction must reach BOTH prompts (and the future API) or the box keeps landing beside the real chip.

The stability fix for multi-part photos: the tool locates each part and crops it at FULL RESOLUTION so each is inspected exactly like a single-part photo (a collage part is no longer judged at 1/N resolution). This discipline must live in the shared system prompt so it reaches the future Anthropic API and can never be silently dropped. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: WHEN THE TOOL PROVIDES PER-PART FULL-RESOLUTION CROPS
results are stable whether one or many parts are uploaded in one image

required.why: In a multi-part collage each part occupies only a fraction of the frame, so fine cues (depth, shadow, texture) shrink and fine categories (dent vs line_mark) get misread even though detection still fires. The engine MUST re-examine each instance at full resolution before classifying, so a part in a collage gets the same scrutiny as a full-frame single-part photo. Pinned so this can never be dropped from the shared system prompt. Freeform system_prompt.md prose - pinned by phrase.
must_contain: INSPECT EACH PART AT FULL RESOLUTION
Localise first (find the anomaly), then

required.why: A dent's bent/raised edge catches light as a bright glint that is easily mislabeled as a line_mark (bright scratch), especially at collage scale. The decisive DEPTH/SHAPE test (localised + depression + broken contour -> dent; thin continuous flat line -> line_mark) must reach BOTH prompts and the future API.

The reciprocal of dent.disambiguation: a line_mark must be FLAT and depth-less, not a localised bright glint on a deformed edge. Without this the engine calls a dent a line_mark. Guards the same line_mark.disambiguation field as line_mark.disambiguation, for the dent concern.

The cup bore's roundness must be assessed on EVERY cup (a pinched/flattened bore is a sev-4 out_of_round), but tilted cups must NOT be over-flagged for mere perspective foreshortening. This decisive test (smooth ellipse under tilt = OK; localised flat/kink = out_of_round) must reach the bundle so the future API both catches genuine ovality and ignores tilt.

Reddish/brown colour at a rim is ambiguous: it is corrosion only on INTACT metal, but is edge_chip (contact/scuff staining) when it sits on a SHEARED/NOTCHED rim where material is missing. Without this, reddish rim damage gets mislabeled corrosion. The edge-outline test must reach the bundle so the future API distinguishes staining from a chip.
